name: Constraint Geology Atlas
purpose: Consolidate simulation evidence from groove formation, decay, reset, recovery, hysteresis, scars, and failure geometry into a governed atlas of constraint-geology structures.

atlas_targets.name: Admissibility Groove Taxonomy
atlas_targets.requirement: Classify stable, fragile, deceptive, residual, and scarred groove structures.

atlas_targets.name: Constraint Scar Mapping
atlas_targets.requirement: Map irreversible or semi-irreversible deformation left by blocker activation.

atlas_targets.name: Recovery Geology
atlas_targets.requirement: Classify whether recovered basins return cleanly, elastically, plastically, or deceptively.

atlas_targets.name: Path-Dependent Basin Stratification
atlas_targets.requirement: Layer basin behavior by recursive history, decay state, and hysteresis class.

atlas_targets.name: Proof Eligibility Terrain
atlas_targets.requirement: Map which constraint-geology structures support review, require review, or block proof use.

geology_classes.meaning: Repeated admissible recursion forms a stable local pathway.
Admissibility pathway exists but remains threshold-sensitive.
Pathway appears stable but later reveals false stability or hidden instability.
Decayed constraint memory weakly biases future admissibility.
Basin recovers with bounded deformation and preserved local admissibility.
Basin recovers but retains lasting path-dependent deformation.
Prior failure geometry activation leaves persistent destabilizing structure.
Topology loses admissibility connectivity or boundary access.
